# Parenting Academy

> Real-world parenting advice from a parent who's still figuring it out. Bedtime routines, picky eaters, screen time, positive discipline — no judgment, no lectures.

Parenting Academy (https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/) is a parenting blog with practical, first-person articles for parents of toddlers and young children. All content is original and written in a warm, honest voice.

## Articles

- [My Toddler Is Suddenly Afraid of the Dark](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/afraid-of-dark/): At 3, my daughter suddenly decided the dark was full of monsters. The nightlight, the room check, and the silly spray that fixed bedtime.
- [Bathtime Went From Favorite to Screaming in a Week](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/bathtime-battles/): She loved baths for two years, then suddenly screamed at the sight of the tub. New toys, pouring games, and not forcing it brought it back.
- [What Finally Fixed Our Toddler Bedtime (It Wasn't a Fancy Routine)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/bedtime-routines-for-toddlers/): Our toddler fought bedtime for months. Here is the simple routine that actually worked — and the mistake I kept making that kept it broken.
- [We Moved Her to a Big Kid Bed and It Was Chaos (Then Fine)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/big-kid-bed/): The first week of midnight wanderings nearly broke us. What helped: the okay-to-wake clock, and a humbling mattress-on-the-floor phase.
- [My Toddler Has Chores and It's Not What You Think](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/chores-for-toddlers/): My three-year-old has exactly two jobs: socks in the basket and wiping the table. The pride on her face is the whole point.
- [I Compared My Kid to Other Kids. I Had to Stop](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/comparing-kids/): The playground comparison trap nearly broke me — someone else's kid counting to fifty while mine ate sand. What I tell myself now when the spiral starts.
- [The Daycare Drop-Off Cry Nearly Broke Me (Then I Fixed the Goodbye)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/daycare-dropoff-cry/): My daughter screamed every morning at daycare drop-off for weeks. The fix was not what the parenting books said — it was making the goodbye shorter and boring.
- [The Nap Is Gone and Nobody Is Okay](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/dropping-the-nap/): The nap vanished at 3 and left 5pm meltdowns behind. Quiet time and an earlier bedtime are what's keeping our family functional.
- [Getting My Toddler Dressed Used to Take 25 Minutes](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/getting-dressed-battles/): Twenty-five minutes to put on a t-shirt and leggings. Bribery flopped, night-before picks got rejected — two real choices and sock puppets saved us.
- [Grandma Undoes All My Rules in One Afternoon](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/grandparents-rules/): One visit from grandma: three biscuits before lunch, bedtime at nine. I stopped fighting it and had the honest talk instead.
- [The Grocery Store Meltdown: What I Do Now (and What I Stopped Doing)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/grocery-store-meltdown/): Public tantrums are the worst parenting stress test. I used to negotiate, threaten, and perform for the audience. Here is the boring routine that actually works now.
- [My 4-Year-Old Lies to My Face Now](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/kid-lying/): My daughter started lying about everything from cookies to crayons on the wall. The interrogation approach flopped — here's what actually made truth-telling safe.
- [Leaving the Playground Without a Meltdown (Usually)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/leaving-playground/): For six months I carried my screaming daughter out of the playground like a rolled-up carpet. Here's what finally made leaving bearable.
- [Our Long Car Ride Survival Kit (Tested on a 6-Hour Drive)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/long-car-rides/): Six hours in the car with a 4-year-old and a 2-year-old. What actually kept them happy, what we packed for nothing, and the backseat rules that saved us.
- [Screen Time Rules That Survived Contact With Our Actual Kids](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/managing-screen-time/): I tried strict screen limits, screen-free weeks, all of it. Here is the imperfect system we landed on — and why the guilt spiral was the real problem.
- [I Stopped Yelling to Get Us Out the Door in the Mornings](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/mornings-without-yelling/): Our mornings used to be a 40-minute shouting match over shoes. Here is the unglamorous system that fixed it — no 5am wake-ups required.
- [The Parent Guilt Never Fully Leaves](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/parent-guilt/): I missed bedtime three nights in a row and the guilt nearly ate me. Overcompensating with toys flopped — here's what actually quieted it.
- [My Kid Ate Nothing But Beige Food for a Year. She's Fine.](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/picky-eaters/): Pasta, bread, crackers, repeat. What I learned about picky eating after a year of beige dinners — and the low-pressure tricks that slowly worked.
- [Positive Discipline, From a Parent Who Used to Yell](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/positive-discipline-basics/): I was a yeller. Here is how I slowly switched to calmer, firmer discipline — the scripts that work, and what I do on the days I still lose it.
- [Potty Training Is Not a Milestone. It's a Negotiation With a Tiny Terrorist.](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/potty-training/): We tried the three-day method, the sticker chart, the peer pressure. What finally worked was stopping all of it. An honest account of potty training a stubborn toddler.
- [Getting Your Firstborn Ready for a New Sibling (What Worked, What Flopped)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/preparing-for-new-sibling/): We tried to prepare our 3-year-old for her baby brother. Some of it helped a lot, some of it backfired. The full honest rundown.
- [Free Printable: Our Toddler Bedtime Routine Chart (Fridge-Tested)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/printable-bedtime-routine-chart/): A free printable bedtime routine chart for toddlers: tidy up, bath, teeth, PJs, story, hugs, lights out. The exact chart on our fridge, and why the checklist mattered more than the routine itself.
- [10 Rainy-Day Activities That Actually Entertained My Toddler](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/rainy-day-activities/): Tested on real rainy Saturdays with my 3-year-old: fort building, tape roads, sink play — plus the three ideas that flopped completely.
- [How We Survive Restaurants With a Toddler (Mostly)](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/restaurant-survival/): The tote bag that lives in our car, why we eat at 5:30, and the anniversary dinner that taught us to just leave when it's not working.
- [Her Lunchbox Came Home Full Every Day. Lunch Was the Wrong Battle.](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/school-lunchbox-picky-eater/): She ate fine at home but her lunchbox came back untouched every day. A pediatric OT helped me stop fighting lunch and start fixing the parts that were actually broken.
- [School Phone Bans Cut Screen Time 15% — and Changed Nothing](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/school-phone-bans/): Kids used their phones 15% less at school after the bans — but their total screen time did not budge. The minutes just moved to social media. Here is what that tells me about my own house.
- [I Stopped Forcing My Toddler to Share](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/sharing-battles/): Forcing my toddler to hand over her shovel bought twenty minutes of screaming for forty seconds of sharing. The timer and the sacred comfort toy work better.
- [My Kids Fight 40 Times a Day](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/sibling-fighting/): My 4-year-old and 2-year-old fight over everything, including air. What's normal, when I step in, and the one rule that cut the battles in half.
- [Sleep Regressions Are Real and I Hate Them](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/sleep-regression/): The two-year sleep regression wrecked us for three weeks. What got us through wasn't a trick — it was lowering the bar everywhere else.
- [My Toddler Hit Other Kids. Here's What Stopped It](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/toddler-hitting/): My 2-year-old started smacking kids at the playground and I wanted to sink into the ground. The calm, firm approach that actually stopped it.
- [Brushing a Toddler's Teeth Without the Nightly Wrestling Match](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/toddler-toothbrushing-battle/): Toothbrushing used to end with one of us crying (me, once). Two toothbrushes and a terrible song fixed it.
- [The Bedtime Stall: 47 Excuses, One Thing That Worked](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/toddler-wont-stay-in-bed/): Nine trips out of bed in one night — water, hugs, monsters, an itchy toe. The ticket system flopped; silent returns and an earlier bedtime fixed it.
- [My Kid Bit Another Kid at the Playground. The Shame Was the Worst Part.](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/when-your-kid-bites/): The bite, the other parent\u2019s face, and what I learned about handling it without the public shaming ritual. Practical, and kinder than the parenting forums.
- [The Whining Phase Nearly Broke Me](https://parenting-academy.pages.dev/posts/whining/): The 6pm whine drilled into my skull for months. Ignoring it backfired, caving trained it — naming the feeling plus one calm redo finally turned it down.
